texts.facts: In this case, a Claim Petition is filed u/s 166(1) MV Act, by the claimant/petitioner/injured. 2. As per the case of the claimant/petitioner, on 03.10.2017 at about 02:15 PM injured/petitioner was going on a motor cycle bearing no. HR51AK8394 via Palla Road, Faridabad Haryana near English Vine Shop at Palla Village Chowk Faridabad Haryana. One truck bearing no. HR38 5212, being driven by respondent no.1 in rash, careless and negligent manner and at very high,fast and violent speed, hit the petitioner. Due to such sudden and forceful impact, the petitioner fell on the road. As a result petitioner sustain grievous injury including on his leg and left side body. He was admitted to Sarvodaya Hospital where he was medically examined and injury was opined as dangerous injury. 3. Accordingly, an FIR was registered. Ultimately the charge sheet u/s. 279, 337 & 338 IPC was filed. 4. Further as per record R-1 and R-2 appeared initially but they did not file any reply and later on stopped appearing . 5. But, as a reply is filed by insurance company/R-3. MACT No.:416/2018 Devender Kumar Vs Jai Singh & ors. Page No. 2 of 24 Insurance of the offending vehicle with R3 is not denied. But it is stated that such insurance liability of R-3is subject to compliance of terms and condition of insurance policy, including holding of valid driving license, permit and fitness certificate. Further income of the petitioner was denied. It is further claimed that accident took place due to so negligence of petitioner only. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 11.04.2019: As per record, claimant examined himself in chief as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/10 relating to his identity and medical treatment and bills. Devendra Kumar vs . Jai Singh & Ors. on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63513448/ 2 8. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioners. 10. Further, as per record, none of the respondent led any evidence. 11. Further, as per record, a medical physical disability MACT No.:416/2018 Devender Kumar Vs Jai Singh & ors . Page No. 3 of 24 certificate, issued by Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya hospital, New Delhi dated 30.04.2019 noting the disability of the present injured/claimant as 48% regarding both low limb. 15. Further, in the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279, 337 & 338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. In the present case also, driver did not enter into the witness box to controvert the claim of petitioner or even to explain circumstances of accident. 17. On perusal of examination-in-chief by way of affidavit of PW-1/injured person, it is noted that PW- 1/Victim/Injured person deposed on the lines of original complaint/stand, which is already Devendra Kumar vs . Jai Singh & Ors. on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63513448/ 3 noted above. It was further deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of the R-1, the accident in question took place. 18. During their cross examination by Ld. Counsel for insurance company, PW-1 taking consistent stand denied the suggestion that accident took place due to his driving.
texts.arguments: 13. On the basis of material on record, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under : Issue No.1 14. Including in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Including in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the MACT No.:416/2018 Devender Kumar Vs Jai Singh & ors. Page No. 4 of 24 offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that including in the case of Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it is held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. 23.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 23.7. 27. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that there is a vagueness in the claim that he is unable to work since the accident and no supporting documents/ witness proved in this regard. It is stated that as such, only a reasonable period for loss of income be granted, if so at all. 28. 34. It is further argued by petitioner side that accordingly functional disability of at least of 48% in relation to whole body be taken in the present case, as he was working as a pujari/priest and same do require constant standing and moving around for long hours each day, from one house to another or even in the temple. 35. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel or insurance company that there is no functional disability of 48% in any case, in the present case. It is further argued that functional disability, if any is much lower. It may be noted that in the judgment of Ram Charan & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. 44. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and MACT No.:416/2018 Devender Kumar Vs Jai Singh & ors. Page No. 16 of 24 the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. In the case of literate persons, it is not mandatory to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. 52. The following conditions are to be adhered to by SBI, Saket Courts, Delhi with respect to the fixed deposits:- (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
